clue.text: Maybe jack's willing to build bridge say

parts.note: a jack is an example of a playing card
game means ready and willing, as in 'game for anything'

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to put up a bridge, and a jack is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' flags the jack as an example of a card; 'bridge' is the definition, the game, not a structure, and 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is one example of a pastime played with a pack of cards.

clue.text: Slides or photographs you could say

indicators.note: you could say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: to shoot is to photograph, so photographs as a verb is shoots

explanation.surface: Someone is discussing slides versus photos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slides' and 'photographs' look like a pair of camera terms; slides here are playground or water slides.
explanation.definitionFit: A chute is a sloping channel things or people slide down.

clue.text: Bird on roof of car, famous old English 22

parts.note: a robin is a bird
a car's hood is its folding roof (or in America the bonnet)

explanation.surface: A bird perches on a car top, and an old English hero is named.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 refers to the answer at 22 down, a celebrated figure of folk tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw of Sherwood Forest is England's most famous figure of folklore.

clue.text: Information I repeated for the spirits

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: repeated means the letter I is written twice

explanation.surface: Information is given twice to ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii, plural of genie, are spirits of Arabian folklore.

clue.text: Plant that's in my control

indicators.note: in places the flower inside the two letters of my

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flowering plant

explanation.surface: A gardener boasts of a plant they control.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastery is command or full control over something.

clue.text: It's inclined to be emphatic

parts.note: describes a typeface whose letters slope and which printers use to stress a word

explanation.surface: Someone tends to speak forcefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' reads as 'tending', but it means literally sloping, like the slanted print used for stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping type is the printer's usual way of putting emphasis on words.

clue.text: Secondary flower

parts.note: read flower as something that flows: a lesser stream feeding a bigger one

explanation.surface: A gardener's second-best bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' here is something that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river or stream that feeds into a larger one is subsidiary to it.

clue.text: Female, over 50 (just!) and cultivated

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals, just over fifty

indicators.note: cultivated suggests working the letters over into a new form

explanation.surface: A refined woman barely past fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges and to NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Huge deficit concealed in mining output

indicators.note: concealed in places the deficit word inside the mining word

parts.note: coal is what a mine produces
a loss is a deficit

explanation.surface: A big shortfall has been hidden in the coal production figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means enormous, like the giant statue the Colossus.

clue.text: Island in elegant setting? Build a town on it!

indicators.note: the island abbreviation sits in the middle of the word for elegant, which acts as its setting

parts.note: urbane means suave and elegant

explanation.surface: An island set amid elegance invites a developer to build a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' confirms URBANE as the surround for IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To urbanise land is to develop it with towns and city buildings.

clue.text: Remarkable message

explanation.surface: A notable communication arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective signal means notable or striking (a signal achievement); as a noun it is a sign conveying information.

clue.text: His fans finally show disapproval

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of fans

explanation.surface: A performer's fans eventually boo him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fans' suggests supporters, who would not disapprove.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences make a sibilant noise to express displeasure.

clue.text: Boredom can be genuine, without limits

indicators.note: can be signals that the letters may be rearranged into another word
dropping the first and last letters of genuine removes its limits

explanation.surface: Tedium may be quite real, and boundless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without limits' leaves ENUIN from genuine, and 'can be' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French-derived word for listless weariness and tedium.

clue.text: Back numbers

parts.note: read as things that numb the back: spinal anaesthetic injections, not old magazine issues

explanation.surface: Old issues of a magazine are on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back numbers' means old issues of a periodical, but read 'numbers' as things that numb.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinal anaesthetic injections, often given in childbirth, deaden sensation in the lower back and body.

clue.text: City where WMDs are stored, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a bomb bay is the compartment of an aircraft holding bombs, weapons of mass destruction

explanation.surface: A city is said to stockpile weapons of mass destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: WMDs are weapons of mass destruction; the bomb bay of a plane holds them, and said quickly it matches the old name of Mumbai.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombay is the former name of Mumbai, a major Indian city.

clue.text: Does she succeed where Canute failed?

definitions.text: Does she succeed where Canute failed?

parts.words: Does she succeed where Canute failed?
parts.note: King Canute famously could not command the tide; the patriotic song says a female figure rules the waves

explanation.surface: A question asks whether some woman wins where a king lost.
explanation.walkthrough: King Canute (Cnut) is said to have failed to hold back the tide; the British song 'Rule, Britannia!' claims she rules the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: The female personification of Britain is sung of as ruling the seas.

clue.text: Sort of talisman left out to give strength

indicators.note: sort of signals that the letters of talisman are to be re-sorted into a new word

explanation.surface: A lucky charm, with something left out, gives strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' says the L is dropped from the rearranged letters of talisman.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the endurance to keep going.

clue.text: One sister and her boyfriend died, drowned

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a nun is a religious sister
a date is a romantic partner one goes out with

explanation.surface: A nun and her lover die by drowning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drowned' means swamped or flooded here, not a death.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooded or overwhelmed, as with water or with letters and demands.

clue.text: Definitely not Henry Vill's opinion

explanation.surface: A comment on the views of a famously large Tudor monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII was notoriously fat, so he was no slim monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense reads as a slim monarch, the opposite of the portly Tudor; the second is a view or belief someone holds.

clue.text: Creator of a north-south divide

parts.note: points to the Roman emperor whose wall runs across northern England, splitting it from Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone is blamed for Britain's economic gap between regions.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'north-south divide' usually means economic inequality in Britain; here it is a literal Roman wall separating north from south.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor ordered a wall built across northern Britain, physically dividing the island.

clue.text: Endless darkness once not far away

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: night is the time of darkness

explanation.surface: An endless darkness was once close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old-fashioned word for near.

clue.text: Timid cat almost gets the giant rodents

parts.note: coy means shy or timid

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for cat is dropped

parts.note: puss is an informal word for a cat

explanation.surface: A shy cat is nearly overcome by enormous rats.
explanation.definitionFit: Coypus are large South American water rodents, also called nutria.

clue.text: A clergyman, not a comedian

indicators.note: not says the letter a is left out of the clergyman word

parts.note: a chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution

explanation.surface: Someone insists a man is a cleric, not a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to deny that the man is a comedian; it says the clergyman loses 'a'. Charlie Chaplin was the silent-film comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was a famed silent-film comic actor.

clue.text: Famous tale of a foot?

explanation.surface: A well-known story about someone's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as LEG END: the foot is at the bottom of the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional story of heroes; the foot is the far extremity of a limb.

clue.text: Drunk again, lost in reminiscences

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Inebriated once more, someone drifts into old memories.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is wistful longing for the past, the mood of fond reminiscing.

clue.text: Some reports read in a nasal voice

indicators.note: in shows the answer is buried within the words nasal voice

explanation.surface: Some reports are read out in a nasal voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reports' means bangs of guns, not documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a burst of reports.

clue.text: Gordon's plan has no time to change

indicators.note: has no signals that a letter is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: Gordon Brown, long the UK Chancellor, presented the annual budget, his financial plan

explanation.surface: A politician's scheme lacks time to be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was the British Chancellor of the Exchequer who set the yearly budget; to budge is to shift or change position.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to shift position or move from a fixed view.

clue.text: Footballers as champions

explanation.surface: Footballers act as champions.
explanation.definitionFit: Defenders in football are called backs; to champion a cause is to support it.

clue.text: Where Americans wait, under control

explanation.surface: Americans waiting their turn are kept orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans queue by standing on line or in line; kept in line means disciplined and under restraint.

clue.text: Formal dress Bond wanted after dark

indicators.note: after places the bond word behind the dark word

parts.note: black means dark
a tie is something that binds, a bond

explanation.surface: James Bond wanted his evening wear after nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond suggests 007, famed for evening wear, but here it is simply a binding tie.
explanation.definitionFit: The dress code for formal evening wear is a dinner jacket with a bow, named for its neckwear.

clue.text: Planetary mass that's semi-liquid metal

parts.note: a glob is a soft blob or lump of viscous stuff
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A semi-liquid metal blob is the size of a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means relating to the whole world, the planet.

clue.text: Ill-balanced team has done badly without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the scrambled word goes around the team
badly signals that the letters of done are put together wrongly

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: An uneven team has played poorly without someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the team; ONED, the anagram of done, goes round SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lopsided contest or argument is unbalanced, favouring one party.
